daily_load_assessment: The athlete has had three consecutive days of zero training load (August 12-14) following a massive four-session, 137-load day on August 11. This block of complete recovery has allowed acute muscle fatigue to dissipate completely, leaving the energy systems primed for a high-intensity stimulus today.
acute_status_assessment_3_weeks: With a 21-day load of 1038 and 16.35 training hours, the athlete has maintained a solid volume. The acute training load (ATL) sits at 57.1 against a chronic training load (CTL) of 40.0, yielding a Form (TSB) of -17.1. This is well within the safe training zone (above the absolute limit of -30) and indicates that while the athlete is in a productive training phase, they are not chronically overtrained.
sport_trend_assessment_6_months: The long-term fitness trend shows a CTL of 40.0. To reach the target milestone of 60, we need to maintain a controlled ramp rate of +1 to +2 CTL per week. The athlete's base is highly supported by consistent e-bike commuting, meaning their aerobic floor is highly developed. This justifies executing highly specific quality sessions to hit the 5km running and 5-min/20-min cycling power goals.
coach_verdict: Based on the three-day recovery window post-August 11, your system is fully primed to execute a high-intensity quality session. Since running quality has been low in the current block (only 3 running sessions out of 17), today's absolute top priority is a high-intensity VO2max running interval session to target your 5km pace milestone. If joint fatigue feels high, pivot to the cycling interval option.

priority_1.workout_details:
Warm-up: 15 minutes of progressive Zone 2 jogging, followed by 3x30-second strides.
Intervals: 5x1000m at target 5km pace (aim for high leg turnover and smooth posture). Rest: 3 minutes of slow walking recovery between intervals.
Cool-down: 10 minutes of easy jogging.
priority_1.reason: This session addresses the 5km running goal. Following 3 days of rest, your neuromuscular system is fresh, making this the perfect time to recruit fast-twitch fibers and push VO2max adaptations without risking injury.

priority_2.workout_details:
Warm-up: 15 minutes advancing from Zone 1 to Zone 3, including 3x30-second high-cadence spins.
Main Set: 4x5 minutes at 280W (112% FTP) with 5 minutes of easy active recovery spinning (Zone 1) between efforts.
Cool-down: 10 minutes of light spinning below 100W.
priority_2.reason: Directly targets your specific milestone of 5-minute cycling power. The ample rest interval (1:1 work-to-rest ratio) ensures you can sustain high wattages on each repetition to maximize cardiac stroke volume adaptations.

priority_3.workout_details:
Warm-up: 10 minutes of dynamic mobility and core activation.
Main Lift: Barbell Back Squat - 4 sets x 5 reps at 80% 1RM (heavy load to build cycling torque).
Superset 1: Heavy Kettlebell Swings (20kg) - 3 sets x 15 reps + Barbell Bench Press - 3 sets x 8 reps.
Superset 2: Heavy Sandbag carries (70kg) - 3 sets x 50 meters + Hanging Leg Raises - 3 sets x max reps.
Cool-down: 5 minutes of stretching.
priority_3.reason: A highly effective alternative that builds sport-specific lower-body torque for cycling and core stability for running posture, while satisfying your aesthetic goals for the chest, shoulders, and abs.
